messages:
alex: quick heads-up — running `terraform plan` against staging and it shows the canary ConfigMap will be replaced and that forces the Deployment to recreate. we didn't change the CM in this PR, can someone eyeball? :eyes:

mika: can you paste the plan snippet?

alex: sure, excerpt below:

```
# module.k8s.kubernetes_config_map.canary will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_config_map" "canary" {
    ~ metadata = {
        + annotations = {
            + "rollout-timestamp" = "2024-11-13T15:22:00Z"
          }
      }
  }

# module.k8s.kubernetes_deployment.app must be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_deployment" "app" {
    ~ spec = {
        + template {
            + metadata {
                + annotations = {
                    + "deployment.kubernetes.io/revision" = "2"
                  }
              }
          }
      }
  }
```

sam: two quick guesses: 1) CI or kustomize is stamping `rollout-timestamp` on the live object and terraform's state doesn't match, or 2) provider version changed and now computed fields are in the diff.

jordan: +1. did we bump the kubernetes provider in the last provider bump? that can change which metadata fields are considered computed. also check ownerReferences or managedFields in the live resource — those sometimes cause diffs if provider logic changed.

alex: i checked the PR — only change was in a separate chart; no tf changes. CI does write a `rollout-timestamp` annotation during canary runs. i expected that to be ephemeral and not managed by terraform. but terraform thinks it owns the CM content.

lee: i tried an apply earlier and it hung on refresh then we had to force-unlock the state (i ran `terraform force-unlock`). could that leave orphaned computed values?

mika: force-unlock only affects the lock resource, not state contents. but if an apply was interrupted during refresh, the local state may not have the latest live values. recommended: `terraform import` the live resource into the same address, then `terraform plan` to see real diffs.

alex: doing `terraform state show module.k8s.kubernetes_config_map.canary` now, output snippet:

```
# module.k8s.kubernetes_config_map.canary:
metadata:
  name: canary-config
  namespace: staging
  annotations:
    rollout-timestamp: 2024-11-13T15:22:00Z
data:
  config.yaml: "---
 feature: on
"
```

sam: yep, state has the annotation stamped by CI. if CI keeps changing it we should not manage that annotation via terraform. two options: 1) update tf to ignore changes on `metadata[0].annotations["rollout-timestamp"]` via lifecycle.ignore_changes, or 2) stop having CI mutate the TF-managed ConfigMap and instead have CI write a separate ephemeral ConfigMap or use `kubectl annotate` outside of terraform.

jordan: small note — if you use `lifecycle.ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations]` that will ignore all annotations; fine for canary, but call it out in the PR. better to scope to the key if provider supports it.

alex: trying import approach first so we don't get a noisy recreate in the next apply. running:

```
terraform import module.k8s.kubernetes_config_map.canary staging/canary-config
```

alex: import succeeded. re-running `terraform plan`...

ops-bot: notice: last apply in staging was by @lee at 1734998000, lock released. :white_check_mark:

alex: plan now shows no changes! :tada: looks like the state was stale.

mika: nice. still file a small PR to either ignore that annotation or make the CM fully managed in TF so CI doesn't race with terraform.

lee: fwiw i had to re-run the provider init after the bump (provider v2.8.1). if anyone else sees diffs after import, try `terraform init -upgrade` and `terraform refresh` first.

jordan: also if the resource is being modified by a controller (argocd/k8s operator) you can get ongoing diffs. check `kubectl get deployment -o yaml` for managedFields and make sure no controllers own the CM.

alex: thanks all. i'll open a tiny PR to add `lifecycle.ignore_changes = ["metadata[0].annotations.rollout-timestamp"]` and mention CI team. @mika please review when you have a sec. :pray:

mika: on it. will also ping infra-ci to consider writing the annotation to a different resource.

deploy-bot: heads-up: staging canary apply scheduled at 1735012000 — will wait 10m for manual confirmation.

alex: i'll hold off on merging the staging apply until CI stops stamping that annotation during the window. once PR merged i'll run apply and confirm no recreate. :shipit:

sam: documented approach for similar cases lives in infra/runbooks -> k8s/annotations.md — TL;DR: prefer `ignore_changes` for ephemeral fields or move ephemeral stamping out of TF-managed resources.

ajordan: (minor) if anyone wants me to pair on the PR i can — been bitten by this before.

alex: thanks, will take you up on that if mika is busy. closing the loop here — import+plan fixed the immediate noise, PR coming.
